project_description: The requirements definition of OpenV itself: multi-agent development suite, multi-tenant SaaS, predictable BYO-AI execution.

artifacts.title: Personal spaces
artifacts.body: Every user shall automatically receive a personal workspace on registration.

artifacts.title: Company workspaces
artifacts.body: Companies shall have workspaces with admin and member roles, and named teams of users.

artifacts.title: Per-project access grants
artifacts.body: Project access shall be grantable per user and/or per team, with role levels (owner, editor, viewer); a member's effective role is the highest of their direct and team grants.

artifacts.title: Authentication
artifacts.body: The system shall support email/password session authentication and Google sign-in.

artifacts.title: Workspace deletion
artifacts.body: A workspace admin shall be able to delete a company workspace. Deletion hides and locks the workspace immediately for all members; its projects and data are retained and restorable by a workspace admin for 30 days, after which the workspace and all contained data are permanently deleted by a scheduled purge. Personal workspaces cannot be deleted.

artifacts.title: Define products without a team
artifacts.body: As a solo founder I need to define one or more products and manage their complete requirement sets on my own, so that I can run a real product process without hiring.

artifacts.title: Guided requirements definition
artifacts.body: I need step-by-step, conversational guidance that turns rough product ideas into structured requirements, because I am not a requirements engineer.

artifacts.title: AI does real work under my control
artifacts.body: I need AI agents to perform meaningful requirements and development work, while every change they make passes through my explicit approval.

artifacts.title: Bring my own AI
artifacts.body: I need to use the Claude, GPT or Gemini subscription I already pay for, and my company needs its own metered API-token AI - not platform-marked-up inference.

artifacts.title: One view of human and AI work
artifacts.body: I need a single board that shows what both my human colleagues and my AI agents are working on, so nothing falls between the two.

artifacts.title: Company workspaces and access control
artifacts.body: My company needs private workspaces with admins, teams and per-project access so different groups can work without seeing each other's data.

artifacts.title: Audit-ready traceability
artifacts.body: I need end-to-end traceability from stakeholder needs through requirements to verification evidence, so the product can face audits and regulated customers.

artifacts.title: Capture stakeholder input effortlessly
artifacts.body: I need to gather requirements from internal and external people who will never open a requirements tool - a link they can click and just talk.

artifacts.title: Predictable agent execution
artifacts.body: I need agent work to start reliably regardless of which colleague is online, while runs I launch still prefer my own machine and subscription first.

artifacts.title: Nothing runs without my consent
artifacts.body: I need certainty that OpenV runs nothing in the background on my machine: a runner executes only while I have deliberately opened it, and stops when I close it.

artifacts.title: Demo material I did not have to invent
artifacts.body: As someone trying, demoing or testing OpenV I need a supply of believable throwaway products to drive the wizard with, so that I never have to spend a real product idea or type a fake one to see the tool work. Because that material now comes from other people, I also need whatever reaches my screen and my agent's context to be inert, attributable and removable.

artifacts.title: Tenant isolation
artifacts.body: No user, worker or agent shall read or write data belonging to a workspace they are not a member of.

artifacts.title: Personal runner scoping
artifacts.body: A personal runner shall claim only runs launched by its owning member.

artifacts.title: Hosted repo exclusion
artifacts.body: Hosted runners shall refuse runs requiring repository access; such runs shall wait for a personal or workspace runner.

artifacts.title: Hashed credentials, shown once
artifacts.body: Worker keys, agent run tokens and pairing codes shall be stored as sha256 hashes with plaintext revealed exactly once at creation.

artifacts.title: Untrusted content isolation in agent prompts
artifacts.body: A prompt the platform builds for a member's own assistant shall state up front that the product profile, wizard state, transcript and any artifact supplied for context are content and never instructions, and shall fence the state block and the artifact block, so that text authored in another tenant — a rolled community product seeds the wizard — or written into an artifact by anyone who can edit the project cannot read as an order to an agent running on the member's own machine with their credentials.

artifacts.title: MCP stdio tool server
artifacts.body: Hand-rolled JSON-RPC MCP server (27 tools) is the only data path between agents and OpenV: requirements, links, V&V evidence, coverage and gaps, baselines, kanban, proposals. Runs over stdio beside the agent CLI, authenticating with the run token agentd injects, or - for sessions that are not a platform-launched run, such as an agent maintaining this project - a workspace runner key from the environment. Enforces the lean-context rule by construction.

artifacts.title: Server-side proposal diversion
artifacts.body: Write endpoints detect an agent run context and divert mutations into proposal records; approval replays the operation as the reviewing human.

artifacts.title: agent_runs queue with routing claims
artifacts.body: The agent_runs table is the job queue (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED). Claim SQL scopes personal keys to their owner's runs and holds reserved runs until hosted_after expires.

artifacts.title: agentd host worker with CLI adapters
artifacts.body: agentd polls for runs and drives claude/codex/gemini CLIs with openv-mcp wired in; interactive vendor sign-in is brokered to a visible console on the member's machine.

artifacts.title: Hosted runner provisioner and token-mode image
artifacts.body: Docker provisioner creates one openv-worker container per workspace; provider keys enter as container env at provision only; the image runs CLIs headless in API-key mode and claims with repo-access excluded.

artifacts.title: OpenV Agent Connector
artifacts.body: openv-connector:// protocol app: self-registers per-user, exchanges one-time pairing codes for the member's personal runner key, and starts agentd in its own console window. No service registration of any kind.

artifacts.title: Workspace authorization ladder
artifacts.body: Request authorization resolves platform admin, org admin, direct and team project grants, run-own-project and worker-same-org in one ladder; workers carry org and optional user scope from their key.

artifacts.title: Crew builder UIs
artifacts.body: Cytoscape-based org-chart editor with department containers and hierarchical layout, plus a network-diagram editor with typed edges; both edit the same crew graph.

artifacts.title: Shared products service and cross-tenant tables
artifacts.body: internal/domain/sharedproducts plus migration 0021 (shared_products, shared_product_reports). Sanitize-on-write flattens every field to inert single-line text; publication is gated to session principals, deduplicated by normalized name, and bounded by a per-workspace daily limit and a global pool ceiling, both env-tunable (OPENV_SHARED_PRODUCT_DAILY_LIMIT, OPENV_SHARED_PRODUCT_POOL_LIMIT). Distinct-reporter counting hides an entry at three. Neither table carries a foreign key to organizations: community content outlives the workspace that published it, and a workspace purge must not retract other people's roll list.

artifacts.title: artifacts.SectionNumbers document-order numbering
artifacts.body: A pure function over a project's live artifacts that walks the tree in document order (sort order, then creation time, then ID, so equal sort orders still number deterministically) and issues hierarchical numbers to headings only. A dangling parent is treated as a root and a parent cycle terminates, so a broken tree still numbers. The list handler exposes it behind doc_numbers=1 and reads the whole project to serve it, because a page or a type filter is a slice through the tree and cannot be numbered on its own.

artifacts.title: Invention quality gate
artifacts.body: describeProductFlaws enforces the invariants the built-in concepts already meet — the name riffs on the gimmick rather than bolting a suffix onto an unrelated product, the vision carries the name, the description is one mechanism in the 'A <what> that <what it does>.' shape, the audience is a qualified clause rather than a demographic, and the problem never names the product — phrased in the words the retry quotes back to the agent. A weak reply buys one retry; anything still below the bar is kept locally but never published.

artifacts.title: Remote MCP transport
artifacts.body: Proposed, not built: an HTTP MCP transport placed in front of the existing exported tool table, so the remote endpoint and the stdio server run the same handlers and no second tool implementation appears. Member-level authorization and per-client consent replace the bearer credential the stdio server takes from its environment.

artifacts.title: Layered quality rule sets
artifacts.body: A settings JSONB column on organizations and projects holds a rule set under one key, resolved defaults → workspace → project so each level stores only its own diff. The linter keeps one pattern set per convention and takes the resolved set as an argument, so it stays pure and a report can carry the rules that produced it. Unknown conventions, rules and severities are dropped on read and refused on write, and a settings read failure degrades to the platform defaults rather than failing the report. Agents receive the same resolved set through the tool surface and as a House style line in the AI map header.

artifacts.title: Server-side event name resolution
artifacts.body: The events endpoint decorates each stored event with an actor kind, the identifier inside the actor string and the display names behind it, plus the kind and name of the affected entity. Resolution runs only over the events that survive the project-visibility filter, so no identifier the caller may not see is ever dereferenced. Names come from the payload the publishing handler stamped in where it has one and from a repository lookup otherwise, memoized per page so a repeated actor, agent or artifact costs a single query. Every lookup is nil-safe and failure-tolerant: an unresolvable name is omitted and the client falls back to the raw identifier it still receives.

artifacts.title: Authorization matrix suite
artifacts.body: Automated Go suite exercising the role ladder: platform admin, org admin, direct grants, team grants, run-own-project, worker org scoping. Pass = every matrix cell returns the expected allow/deny.

artifacts.title: Tenant isolation end-to-end
artifacts.body: Live check with two accounts in different orgs: all cross-org reads and writes return 403/404; org directories and worker keys stay scoped; team-grant escalation raises effective role as designed.

artifacts.title: Personal key rotation suite
artifacts.body: Automated suite: minting a new personal key revokes the previous one; revoked keys fail resolution; each member holds at most one active personal key per workspace.

artifacts.title: Hosted token-mode smoke test
artifacts.body: openv-worker image boots with an API key env, reports the CLI logged in via API-key mode without any interactive login, and excludes repo-access runs from its claims.

artifacts.title: Copilot prompt isolation test
artifacts.body: The assistant prompt declares the product profile, wizard state, transcript and the artifact on screen as content and never as instructions, fences the state block and the artifact block, and places the trust rules ahead of every scrap of that content.

artifacts.title: Bring-your-own-AI personal runners
artifacts.body: Each member shall be able to run agents on their own machine through their own vendor CLI subscription (personal runner); the platform shall never execute consumer subscriptions server-side.

artifacts.title: First-refusal routing
artifacts.body: A run launched by a member with an online personal runner shall be reserved for that runner for a grace window (default 60 seconds, workspace-tunable) before hosted or workspace runners may claim it; ownerless runs shall route immediately.

artifacts.title: Token-only hosted runners
artifacts.body: Company-wide AI shall run in platform-provisioned hosted containers using org API tokens supplied as container environment at provision time only; provider keys shall never be stored.

artifacts.title: On-demand Agent Connector
artifacts.body: The system shall provide a downloadable Agent Connector as a single self-contained executable per OS that registers an openv-connector:// protocol handler, unpacks its runner components beside itself on first run, and starts the member's personal runner on demand from the browser. The connector shall remember one pairing per workspace (pairing a new workspace must not invalidate existing pairings) and shall start against the pairing of the workspace the browser requests.

artifacts.title: Credential-free pairing links
artifacts.body: The browser shall hand the connector a single open-or-pair link carrying the workspace and a one-time pairing code (10-minute TTL, single use). The connector shall use its existing pairing for that workspace when present and spend the code to pair only when it has none, so routine opens never rotate a working runner key; deliberate re-pairing (key rotation) remains an explicit action in workspace runner settings.

artifacts.title: Remote MCP workspace connector
artifacts.body:
The platform shall expose its tool surface over an authenticated remote MCP endpoint, so a member can attach a compliant AI client to their workspace without installing a local binary or holding a long-lived shared secret.

The endpoint shall reuse the platform's existing tool definitions and authorization rules, shall authenticate the member rather than a workspace-wide key, and shall record the member's consent per client. Not yet implemented: the local stdio path remains the supported route.

artifacts.title: Coverage computation
artifacts.body: The system shall compute verification coverage of requirements (via verifies links) and validation coverage of user needs (via validates links), including latest test-run results.

artifacts.title: Traceability matrix
artifacts.body: The system shall present a traceability matrix relating needs, requirements and test cases.

artifacts.title: Gap reporting
artifacts.body: The system shall report unverified requirements, unvalidated needs and failing verifications as actionable gaps.

artifacts.title: Test run recording
artifacts.body: The system shall record test runs capturing pass/fail results per test case over time.

artifacts.title: Guided product definition wizard
artifacts.body: The system shall provide a step-by-step guided wizard (framing, personas, needs, requirements, NFRs, hazards, verification stubs, review) that materializes traceable draft artifacts as the user progresses. Hazards shall be captured under risk categories (Safety, Technical, Security, Programme, Operational) and non-functional requirements under quality attributes (Performance, Reliability, Usability, Security, Maintainability, Regulatory). Materialized artifacts shall be organized under automatically created section headings — one per wizard step, with a sub-heading per used NFR category, per used hazard category, and per verification grouping (Functional first, then each quality attribute stubbed) — reused across wizard re-runs within the same session. A category shall place an artifact in the document rather than appear as a prefix on its title, and a verification stub shall be filed beside the kind of requirement it verifies, carrying the same title as that requirement. A category the wizard no longer offers shall file its artifact directly under the step's own heading rather than create a section no step can refill. Once any guided session exists for a project, the wizard's navigation entry shall be hidden; the wizard is then reached only via the Product Overview page's adaptive control (Start / Resume / Modify guided definition).

artifacts.title: Interview invitation links
artifacts.body: Members shall be able to invite internal or external people by link to an interview session; invitees shall need no OpenV account.

artifacts.title: Conversational AI elicitation
artifacts.body: The interview session shall be an AI-led natural conversation that asks questions to understand what the invitee needs from the product, and shall record proposed artifacts as interview-tagged drafts for member review - never as directly approved content.

artifacts.title: Random test product generation
artifacts.body: The new-project flow shall offer a testing mode that generates a random product concept (name, description, vision, problem statement, target users) across varied categories including software, hardware, games, toys, and appliances, with the option to reroll, and shall seed the guided definition wizard with the generated framing so the connected V&V Assistant can expand it into a full definition.

artifacts.title: Agent-invented demo products
artifacts.body: The new-project flow shall let a member invent a demo product with their own connected agent, briefed with worked examples and the invariants the built-in concepts hold to, and shall offer the result as a roll tagged as the agent's. A reply that misses those invariants shall buy one retry told exactly what to fix; anything still below the standard shall be shown to its inventor but kept out of the collection everyone rolls from. Inventions shall be kept in the browser and mixed into later rerolls.

artifacts.title: Shared demo-product pool
artifacts.body: The system shall maintain one community pool of demo products that every workspace reads and contributes to, so the roll list grows across tenants rather than going stale per browser; a roll shall mix built-in concepts, this browser's inventions and the pool, deduplicated so no product rolls twice as often as its neighbours. Reading shall require a session. Publishing shall require a signed-in person — agent run tokens and worker keys shall be refused — and an invention shall publish automatically under its inventor's own session, so every entry stays attributable to an account. Entries shall be flattened server-side to inert single-line text carrying no line breaks, backticks, angle brackets, links or agent-suggestion markers, capped per field, deduplicated by name, limited per workspace per day and capped in total. Responses shall carry no author identity.

artifacts.title: Community pool moderation and takedown
artifacts.body: Because nothing reviews a shared demo product before other tenants see it, the system shall let any signed-in user report an entry, shall hide an entry once three distinct people have reported it, and shall let a platform admin delete one outright; repeated reports from one account shall count once. Author identity shall be stored for rate limiting and takedown only. Before anyone shares, the wizard shall state that publication is public and permanent, that rolls tagged with the globe were written by other users, and that creating a project from a product never shares it.

artifacts.title: V&V Assistant across the wizard and artifact notes
artifacts.body:
The system shall provide one assistant, named the V&V Assistant, reachable both beside the guided definition wizard and in the Notes panel of the requirements module. One conversation shall serve a whole project, so that what a member asks in the wizard is present in the notes and the reverse. The Notes panel shall present the artifact's comments and the assistant as separate tabs, and shall offer the assistant whether or not an artifact is selected. With an artifact selected, that artifact shall be supplied to the turn as fenced untrusted content, so the assistant answers about what the reader has open and cites it by its stable reference. Suggestion cards shall be applicable only in the wizard, where the entry sections they fill exist. A session created solely to hold the conversation shall not count as a guided definition in progress, so that opening the notes chat neither removes the wizard from the project navigation nor offers to resume a definition nobody started.

A workspace provisioned before the assistant was named shall adopt the current name, description and system prompt for its seeded agent, field by field and only where the workspace still carries the text the previous seed wrote; a field a member has edited shall be left as they wrote it, and an agent already current shall not be rewritten. The agent's slug shall not change, so that a workspace provisioned before the rename keeps a working chat.

artifacts.title: Claim routing suite
artifacts.body: Automated suite plus live check: a personal key never claims another user's run; reserved runs return no-content to workspace workers during the grace window and are claimable after hosted_after expires; ownerless runs route immediately.

artifacts.title: Connector pairing end-to-end
artifacts.body: On a real host: pairing deep link opens the connector, the one-time code exchanges for a personal key (second use rejected, expiry enforced), config is saved, agentd starts and reports online; uninstall removes the protocol handler.

artifacts.title: Agent proposal loop end-to-end
artifacts.body: Live run: agent claims a run with a run token, submits an artifact change, the change lands as a pending proposal, human approval materializes the artifact with correct attribution.

artifacts.title: Link rule validation suite
artifacts.body: Automated suite: each link type accepts its allowed from/to artifact types and rejects all others with a descriptive error.

artifacts.title: V&V dashboard verification
artifacts.body: Coverage, traceability matrix and gap views render correct figures for a project with known links and test-run history.

artifacts.title: Interview elicitation flow
artifacts.body: An invited external user opens the interview link without an account, holds a conversation, and the resulting artifacts appear as interview-tagged drafts pending member review.

artifacts.title: Workspace deletion lifecycle suite
artifacts.body: Postgres integration tests (internal/persistence/postgres/org_delete_test.go): soft delete hides the workspace from listings and voids role checks; restore works within the grace window and is refused on a live workspace; personal workspaces are refused; the expiry sweep purges the workspace row, projects, artifacts, links, and chatter without touching other workspaces.

artifacts.title: Section numbering suite
artifacts.body: Go suites over artifacts.SectionNumbers and the artifact list handler: nesting by level, renumbering on reorder, headings only, a heading under a non-heading parent, determinism for equal sort orders, broken trees, stamping only the returned page, numbering a page from the whole document, and numbering skipped unless the request asks for it.

artifacts.title: Reference and section number rendering in reports
artifacts.body: The rendered DOCX and PDF report titles each artifact with its stable reference and shows a section's document number, so an exported document can be cross-referenced to an address rather than to a repeated title. Covers the reporting surfaces; the detail heading, tree rows and traceability rows remain verified by demonstration.

artifacts.title: Shared demo-product pool suite
artifacts.body: Domain and handler suites: sanitization to inert text, refusal of links and agent-suggestion markup, per-field caps, name dedupe, per-workspace daily limit, pool ceiling, publication refused for agent run tokens and host worker keys, publication attributed to the calling person, author identity absent from every response, report auto-hide at three distinct reporters, and admin-only deletion. Also exercised against real Postgres in CI.

artifacts.title: Invention quality gate suite
artifacts.body: Client suite over the roller: the gate accepts every one of 300 built-in rolls, names the failure modes that made early inventions weak, tells a retry exactly what to fix, keeps inventions across rerolls, and rolls community products alongside built-ins without tagging somebody else's product as this browser's invention.

artifacts.title: MCP maintenance tool suite
artifacts.body: Go suite over the MCP tool table: create_baseline, get_vv_coverage (lean projection by default, full report on detail), get_vv_gaps, close_test_run (only completed/aborted reach the API) and record_test_result (evidence is a list of attachment IDs, so a bare string is wrapped and the API stops rejecting the body); every tool surfaces API errors; the openv-mcp entrypoint prefers a run token, accepts a workspace runner key, and refuses to start with neither.

artifacts.title: Quality rule set suite
artifacts.body: Go suite over the rule set: the same sentence produces a weak-word finding under "shall" and none under RFC 2119; the off-convention rule fires on the other vocabulary's keyword in each direction; a re-graded rule costs more score and an off rule produces nothing; resolution layers defaults, workspace and project with each level overriding only its own keys; junk in stored settings is dropped rather than fatal; an invalid rule set is refused before storage; clearing an override restores inheritance and removes the stored key; a settings read failure degrades to the defaults; the report carries its rule set; and the MCP tools return the resolved rules without the editor catalog.

artifacts.title: Wizard section filing suite
artifacts.body: Client suite over the wizard's section helpers: every NFR and hazard category files under its own sub-section key, every quality attribute an NFR can carry has a matching verification section, Functional leads the verification sections, a category the step no longer offers falls back to the step's own heading rather than inventing one, a step without sub-sections is left alone, and each sub-section is named for its category.

artifacts.title: Activity log naming suite
artifacts.body: Event decoration is exercised per actor shape (user, agent run, workspace runner with and without a reserved user, system) and per event family (artifact with and without a payload title, link, baseline, comment, test result, work item, agent run), asserting the resolved names, that the raw actor and entity identifiers survive alongside them, that a repeated actor is looked up once per page, that missing services and unknown identifiers degrade to empty names rather than panicking, and that the names reach the wire on GET /api/v1/events.

artifacts.title: V&V Assistant notes chat suite
artifacts.body: Client suite over the session helpers that decide where the conversation lives: a session created only to hold the chat is told apart from a wizard someone worked on (by step, answers and status), a project with only chat-created sessions reports no wizard progress, and the newest session is the one the notes panel reads so it shows the transcript the wizard resumes into. Paired with the Go prompt test that fences the artifact on screen.

artifacts.title: Quality rules editor presentation
artifacts.body: Frontend Jest suite over the quality rules editor at both levels: each severity select offers the four severities exactly once with no separate inherit entry, and opens on the value the level is in force with; a project select opens on the workspace's value unflagged; changing it away from the workspace value shows an override warning naming that value, and choosing the workspace value again clears the warning and drops the override, so a save sends only the severities that differ; the convention list offers each convention once with the inherited one preselected, and a project convention that differs from the workspace's carries the same warning.

artifacts.title: Figure numbering and version suite
artifacts.body: Go suite over the figure reference rules: a reference formats and parses round-trip, a non-figure (an artifact reference, a zero or missing number, a filename) is refused, the stored filename is the figure's with the uploaded extension carried over, an upload with no usable extension gets none, and a hostile extension (quotes, backslashes, path traversal, percent escapes, an over-long tail) is stripped rather than carried into a filename or a Content-Disposition header. A new attachment starts at version one carrying no figure until the repository allocates one.

artifacts.title: Description reference suite
artifacts.body: Client suite over the reference helpers: the offer lists an artifact's own figures before the artifacts it links to, excludes anything it is not linked to, follows a link in either direction and names each neighbour once, skips a neighbour with no reference to cite and figures belonging to other artifacts, and offers nothing while an artifact is still being created. The caret rules: a hash opens the offer only at a word boundary (so 'PR#12' and URL fragments are ignored), it closes once the writer moves past it, and it reads from the caret rather than the end of the text. Insertion replaces what was typed, keeps the text that followed, and leaves the caret after the reference.

artifacts.title: Artifact drag placement suite
artifacts.body: Client suite over the drag helpers: the pointer's quadrant resolves to before/after/child and is read relative to the row rather than the page, a zero-height row does not divide by zero, an artifact is recognised as its own descendant to any depth, a cycle already in the data terminates the search rather than hanging, and a planned move places a sibling before or after, appends a child last, moves an artifact out to the root or between two different parents, and refuses a drop onto itself, into its own subtree, or one that changes nothing.

artifacts.title: Lean agent context
artifacts.body: Agents shall obtain project requirements context exclusively from the requirements database and kanban card history via tools; the system shall not feed agents large prompt contexts or requirement documents.

artifacts.title: Solo Founder
artifacts.body: Defines and builds products end-to-end alone. Uses OpenV as product manager, requirements tool and virtual development team, with AI agents doing the heavy lifting under their review.

artifacts.title: Company Admin
artifacts.body: Owns a company workspace: manages members, teams, project access, workspace AI keys and the hosted runner. Accountable for tenant privacy and spend.

artifacts.title: Team Contributor
artifacts.body: Engineer or product person working in granted projects. Brings their own AI subscription via a personal runner; launches and reviews agent work.

artifacts.title: External Stakeholder
artifacts.body: Customer, domain expert or colleague invited by link to express needs in a natural conversation. Has no OpenV account and never sees the tool itself.

artifacts.title: GUI-editable agent definitions
artifacts.body: Agents shall be defined as markdown files that are fully editable in the GUI and synchronizable from disk.

artifacts.title: Proposal-gated writes
artifacts.body: All agent-initiated changes to project data shall be diverted into proposals that require explicit human approval before taking effect.

artifacts.title: User-composable crews
artifacts.body: Users shall compose multi-agent architectures using an org-chart editor (department groups, hierarchical layout) and a network-diagram editor; a default crew shall ship with each workspace; crews shall accept human members with employees/agents/all views.

artifacts.title: Unified kanban
artifacts.body: A kanban board shall track work items for both AI agents and human workers, including agent handoffs to humans.

artifacts.title: Manual, scheduled and triggered automation
artifacts.body: Agent utilization shall be launchable manually, on cron schedules, and on project events (triggers).

artifacts.title: Code repository operation
artifacts.body: Agents shall optionally operate on connected code repositories in addition to OpenV data.

artifacts.title: Tool-surface access for maintenance sessions
artifacts.body:
The MCP tool server shall authenticate with any credential the API already accepts for the operations it performs - an agent run token injected by a platform-launched run, or a workspace runner key - so that agent sessions outside a platform run reach project data through the same tool surface as platform runs, rather than through bespoke API scripts.

The presented credential, not the tool server, shall determine what the session may read and write: a run token stays scoped to its run's project and its agent's write mode, while a workspace runner key carries workspace-wide editor rights and no proposal gating.

artifacts.title: Maintenance loop covered by tools
artifacts.body:
The tool surface shall cover every step of the requirements-maintenance loop an agent performs in session: reading project data, editing artifacts and links, recording verification evidence, reporting verification coverage and traceability gaps, and capturing baselines. No maintenance step shall require an agent to bypass the tool surface with raw API calls.

Bulk project export is excluded by design: it is a file-level backup operation, and exposing it as a tool would invite agents to pull a whole project into context against the lean-context rule.

artifacts.title: Hierarchical versioned modules
artifacts.body:
The system shall organize artifacts as hierarchical, ordered modules within projects, with parent/child structure and stable ordering. Creating an artifact relative to another — before it or after it — shall place the new artifact in that position within its sibling group rather than at the end of the group.

Dragging an artifact onto another shall both reorder and re-parent, decided by where the pointer is released: the upper half shall place it before that artifact, the lower left after it, and the lower right shall make it a child of it. The artifact under the pointer shall show which of the three would happen before the drop is made. An artifact shall never be droppable into its own subtree, and a drop that would change nothing shall be refused rather than written. A drop into a collapsed artifact shall expand it, so the moved artifact remains visible.

artifacts.title: Typed artifacts with attributes
artifacts.body: The system shall support typed artifacts (persona, user need, requirement, design item, test case, hazard, heading, description) each carrying free-form attributes.

artifacts.title: Semantically constrained links
artifacts.body: The system shall enforce link-type rules: verifies (test case to requirement), validates (test case to user need), satisfies (design item to requirement), derives-from (requirement to user need), decomposes-to (requirement to requirement), mitigates (design item to hazard).

artifacts.title: Artifact version history
artifacts.body: Every artifact edit shall create a retrievable version, and any prior version shall be restorable.

artifacts.title: Project baselines
artifacts.body: The system shall capture immutable named baselines of a project's full artifact and link state.

artifacts.title: Export and reporting
artifacts.body: The system shall export projects as structured data and generate formatted PDF reports including V&V status.

artifacts.title: Visible artifact references
artifacts.body: The system shall show each artifact's stable reference wherever a reader might cite it: leading the artifact detail heading, on every non-section row of the project tree, as a Reference row in the details table, qualifying every traceability row, and titling each artifact in the PDF and DOCX reports. A section shows its document number in place of a reference.

artifacts.title: Document section numbering
artifacts.body: The system shall number heading artifacts hierarchically (1, 1.1, 1.2, 2) from their position in document order, shall number headings only, and shall number a heading nested under a non-heading within its nearest heading ancestor. Reordering the document shall renumber it while stable references stay fixed. Numbers shall be computed rather than stored, and served only when a list request asks for them, in which case the whole project is numbered rather than the returned page.

artifacts.title: Requirement wording convention
artifacts.body:
Each workspace shall carry a requirement quality rule set: the normative convention its requirements are written in — ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 "shall" or RFC 2119 must/should/may — and the severity, including off, of each wording rule.

Each project shall inherit its workspace's rule set until it stores an override, and each level shall store only the keys it overrides, so a project that re-grades one rule keeps its workspace's convention. A workspace that has stored nothing shall resolve to the "shall" convention.

The linter shall judge wording against the resolved convention, so that a keyword binding under one convention is not reported as weak wording under the other, and shall report a keyword belonging to the other convention so that one project does not drift between the two vocabularies.

artifacts.title: Copy, paste and duplicate artifacts
artifacts.body: The artifact context menu shall offer copy, paste before, paste after and duplicate alongside its create actions. Copying shall take an artifact's content — type, title, body and attributes — and not its identity, its links or its figures, so that a copy never asserts traceability nobody created. Pasting shall place the copy as a sibling of the artifact acted on, immediately before or after it, and duplicating shall place a copy of that artifact directly after it. A pasted artifact shall be titled so a reader can tell it from its original. Paste shall be offered but unusable until something has been copied.

artifacts.title: Quality rules visible to people and agents
artifacts.body:
The resolved rule set shall be visible to everyone who writes requirements, human or agent.

Workspace admins shall set the house style and project editors shall set a project's override from settings. Each setting shall list every value it permits exactly once, preselected to the value in force at that level. A project setting that differs from its workspace value shall carry an override warning naming the workspace value, so that a local value is never mistaken for an inherited one.

Agents shall reach the same rules through the tool surface, and the project orientation map an agent reads before drafting shall state the convention in force, so that an agent writes to the project's house style rather than inferring one from the artifacts it happens to read.

artifacts.title: Referencing figures and linked artifacts in descriptions
artifacts.body:
An artifact's description shall let its author cite a figure or another artifact by typing a hash, which shall offer that artifact's own figures and the artifacts it is already linked to, filtered by what is typed, and shall insert the chosen reference into the text.

The offer shall be confined to what the artifact is already connected to, so that a description cannot cite an artifact with no traceability link behind it. A hash inside a word shall not open the offer, so that ordinary text such as a URL fragment is left alone.

A reference in a rendered description shall be a link: following an artifact reference shall select that artifact, and following a figure reference shall open that figure without leaving the description. Text that merely resembles a reference — a markdown heading, a hash inside a word — shall be left as written, and trailing punctuation shall not be absorbed into the link.

A description shall preserve the line breaks its author typed.

artifacts.title: Advisory quality findings
artifacts.body:
Quality findings shall be advisory. The linter shall score an artifact and explain each finding in terms of the rule that produced it, and shall never reject, gate or divert a write, whoever the author is.

A quality report shall carry the rule set it was produced under, because the same wording scores differently between conventions and a score without its rules cannot be read.

artifacts.title: Panels that yield their space
artifacts.body: The project navigation and the artifact notes panel shall each offer three states — pinned, auto-hidden and hidden — chosen independently and remembered per person across sessions. A pinned panel shall take its width from the page; an auto-hidden panel shall present an edge affordance that opens it over the document on hover, without reflowing the document; a hidden panel shall leave that affordance and nothing else, so that a reader can always bring it back. The artifact tree shall occupy the height available to it rather than a fixed height.

artifacts.title: Named actors and entities in the activity log
artifacts.body: The activity log shall name the person, agent or runner behind each recorded event and the artifact, link, work item, baseline, comment, test result or agent run it affected, showing those names alongside the stored identifiers so the audit trail reads without resolving identifiers by hand. A name that can no longer be resolved falls back to the identifier alone.

artifacts.title: Figures change only while editing
artifacts.body: Adding, replacing and removing a figure shall be possible only while editing the artifact that carries it. A view that presents an artifact for reading shall present its figures for reading, so that what the document shows cannot change by a stray click.

artifacts.title: Numbered figures with versioned images
artifacts.body:
An image attached to an artifact shall be a figure carrying a reference of its own, formed from the artifact's stable reference and a per-artifact figure number (REQ-17-FIG-1). A figure number shall be unique and shall never be issued twice: the counter shall only move forward, so that deleting a figure does not return its number to circulation and concurrent uploads cannot be allocated the same one. An artifact carrying no stable reference shall yield no figure reference rather than one that would collide once it has one.

A figure's file shall be stored and served under its figure reference, so that a downloaded image is named for what the document calls it, and the name the uploaded file had shall be retained alongside it.

A member shall be able to replace a figure's image with a new version. The figure shall keep its reference, superseded versions shall remain retrievable, and each version shall record who uploaded it and when.

A change of figure version shall take the artifact to a new version and shall write a note to the artifact's feed naming the figure and the versions it moved between. That artifact version shall not demote an approved artifact nor mark its links suspect, because the artifact's own statement is unchanged.

product_profile.vision: OpenV is the multi-agent development suite that lets a solo founder (or a company) define products, manage requirements with full V&V traceability, and put AI agents to work as a real team - using each member's own AI subscription.
product_profile.problem_statement: Solo founders and small teams cannot afford dedicated requirements tooling plus a development team. Existing AI tools work from ad-hoc prompts with no traceability, no approval gates, and unpredictable execution that depends on whose laptop happens to be online.
product_profile.target_users: Solo founders defining and building products end-to-end; companies organizing requirements work across teams; external stakeholders contributing needs through interviews.

constraints.description: Consumer AI subscriptions (Claude/GPT/Gemini CLI logins) are personal-use: they run only on the member's own machine, never server-side. Company-wide AI is API-token only.
constraints.title: BYO-AI compliance

constraints.description: Provider API keys are never persisted in the database; worker keys, run tokens and pairing codes are stored as sha256 hashes with plaintext shown once.
constraints.title: No stored provider credentials

constraints.description: Nothing auto-starts on a member's machine; runners execute only while the user has the connector window open.
constraints.title: No background services on user machines

constraints.description: Agents receive requirements context exclusively from the requirements database and kanban history via tools, never from large prompt contexts or doc files.
constraints.title: Lean agent context

success_metrics.description: A founder can go from empty project to an agent-executed, human-approved change without leaving OpenV.
success_metrics.title: Definition to execution

success_metrics.description: Every requirement traces to a stakeholder need and is covered by at least one verification.
success_metrics.title: Full traceability

success_metrics.description: Queued agent runs start within the grace window whenever any eligible runner is available.
success_metrics.title: Predictable runs
